A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. All supplied pages were inspected, including v1 Appendices A–B; their contents were matched to retained, revised or removed material in v3, which has no separate appendices.

before.justification: Section 8 reports three original Monte Carlo studies of Bernoulli prediction, sequential testing and conformal coverage, with results in Tables 4–6.

after.justification: Section 8 retains the three original Monte Carlo studies and reports revised numerical results in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: The work remains a theoretical analysis of existing prediction and inference procedures. The predictive-system tuple and new separation witnesses revise the formal framework, without introducing a new predictive algorithm. The experimental Bayes predictor, likelihood-ratio construction and conformal procedure are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Bernoulli prediction and testing tasks and the same heteroskedastic Gaussian conformal scenarios involving Uniform and Beta covariates. The removed Gaussian location laboratory was analytical, not an additional empirical dataset or simulation.

E2.justification: The simulations retain Bayes versus plug-in MLE and likelihood-ratio e-process versus five-look z-testing. Clipping is presented as numerical handling of the MLE comparison. KT, discounted e-processes and dogmatic-prior predictors are theoretical witnesses, not new experimental baseline competitors.

E3.justification: The reported log-loss evaluation separates clipped numerical loss from theoretical unclipped risk, and the boundary diagnostic changes from an empirical frequency to an exact model probability. Sample sizes, testing thresholds, peeking schedule and conformal calibration/test sizes remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether v1 already used clipping internally.

E4.justification: v3 adds an analytical failure check for fixed clipping: Table 2 states that it destroys plug-in martingale self-consistency and permits CApp feasibility only on the restricted parameter interval. Section 8.1 also quantifies boundary events below Monte Carlo resolution. The existing conformal covariate-shift analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state 10,000 Monte Carlo replications. Neither reports seeds, confidence intervals, standard errors or significance tests, and v3 establishes no increase in repeated runs or new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The central risk table is substantially corrected: v1 Table 4 reports finite MLE risk, including 2.368 at n=5; v3 Table 3 reports clipped risk 1.286 and theoretical unclipped risk infinity at every n. These are differently specified quantities, not a same-setting performance gain. Under retained settings, e-process/peeking rejection rates change from 0.034/0.169 to 0.031/0.165, and conformal coverages change from 0.897/0.964/0.888 to 0.900/0.946/0.900.

T1.justification: v3 replaces risk-set closedness with upper-hull closedness, adds support/continuity conditions for Bayes admissibility, and replaces v1's varying-prior martingale equivalence under every true law with a single-prior implication under the prior predictive law. It revises AV dominance and restricts the martingale equivalence to point nulls. New definitions and proofs introduce rank-family coverage efficiency, the predictive-system space, active-coordinate separation witnesses and precise CApp feasibility. The Gaussian separation proposition and formal Lagrangian proposition are removed; appendix proofs are partly relocated and substantially superseded.

C1.justification: v1 claims incompatible geometries, no common refinement and no procedure satisfying all four criteria. v3 instead claims non-nesting of componentwise classes, explicitly permits compatible guarantees and replaces 'No universal procedure' with 'No universal certificate.' The abstract also withdraws martingale necessity for general Blackwell admissibility and qualifies the coverage and approachability claims.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes empirical calibration from self-predictive martingale coherence and explains why calibration does not imply log-loss optimality. It interprets constrained Bayes as separate criterion-specific optimization problems and explains compatibility despite non-nesting. Applications become motivations, Gaussian extensions require further verification, and covariate-shift overcoverage is explicitly interpreted outside the exchangeability guarantee.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the clipping transformation and epsilon=10^-6, identifies simulated versus theoretical table quantities, and documents initialization and split-conformal rank/tie-breaking details. These improve technical specification; they do not establish how v1's computations were implemented. No code or data-access resource is added.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from incompatible paradigms and a purported counterexample to martingale posteriors toward qualified, modular certificate transfer. v3 adds an explicit comparison with Choe and Ramdas on filtration transport and draws on Dawid, Krichevsky–Trofimov and misspecification literature. It removes the companion-paper framing and associated citations, alongside the Blackwell lecture framing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions and discussion are extensively rewritten. Sections 4–6 gain substantial explanatory structure, terminology and scope remarks; proofs previously deferred to appendices appear alongside revised statements. The Gaussian laboratory and duality subsection disappear, and Applications becomes Motivations and Interpretations.

P2.justification: Several diagrams are redrawn or relabelled, especially the explicitly schematic risk plot and simplified coverage plot. The procedure-to-geometry diagram is removed, and the constrained-Bayes diagram is reorganized. The extended classification table is removed, a separation-witness table is added, and the classification and log-loss tables receive substantial structural revisions.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves the alignment of claims, proofs and numerical evidence. It corrects v1's inference from non-nesting to incompatibility, distinguishes the laws supporting martingale statements, supplies missing qualifications for Bayes admissibility, and resolves the finite-versus-infinite MLE risk presentation. The explicit separation witnesses strengthen the central argument. Generality is reduced, including withdrawal of the Gaussian extension, but this trades unsupported breadth for more defensible conclusions.
